name: CTO core vocabulary
description: The 100 terms a technology leader needs to know, from engineering manager to CTO.

cards.subject: technology strategy
says: sets how technology will help the organisation reach its goals
chooses where to invest and what to leave alone
cards.use: need to explain how technology supports the business goals over the next few years
not: lists the tasks of one team for the next sprint

cards.subject: roadmap
says: shows the planned direction and sequence of work over time
is a plan for outcomes that changes as priorities change
cards.use: need to show stakeholders what is planned and in what order
not: is a fixed contract of dates and features that cannot change

cards.subject: OKR
says: pairs an ambitious objective with measurable key results
is reviewed regularly to show progress
cards.use: want a team's goals to be ambitious and measurable
not: is a legal obligation written into a supplier contract

cards.subject: build versus buy
says: is the decision whether to make a capability in-house or acquire it
weighs differentiation, cost, speed and long-term control
cards.use: need to decide whether to write your own tool or purchase one
not: is the choice of which cloud region to use

cards.subject: vendor lock-in
says: makes it costly to switch away from a supplier
grows when your data and code depend on one provider's proprietary features
cards.use: worry that moving away from a supplier later would be very expensive
not: is a contract term that guarantees a price for several years

cards.subject: technology radar
says: tracks technologies and places each as adopt, trial, assess or hold
helps an organisation choose what to use and what to avoid
cards.use: need a shared view of which technologies to adopt or avoid
not: is a tool that monitors servers for outages

cards.subject: platform team
says: builds shared tools and services that other teams use
aims to make other teams faster and more consistent
cards.use: want other teams to stop rebuilding the same tools
not: owns a single customer-facing feature from end to end

cards.subject: core versus context
says: separates what makes the business different from what everyone needs
suggests putting scarce talent on the core and buying the context
cards.use: need to decide where scarce engineers should spend their time
not: separates production from test environments

cards.subject: time to market
says: is how long it takes to get an idea from concept to customers
is shortened by removing delays and limiting work in progress
cards.use: need to judge how quickly a new product can reach customers
not: is the total price of owning a product

cards.subject: Wardley map
says: maps components by user need and how evolved they are
helps show what to build, buy or leave to the market
cards.use: want to see how components evolve and where to invest
not: is a diagram of the servers in a data centre

cards.subject: enterprise architecture
says: describes how an organisation's business, data, applications and technology fit together
guides decisions that span several teams
cards.use: need a view of how all of the organisation's systems relate
not: describes the code structure of one application

cards.subject: reference architecture
says: is a proven template that teams use as a starting point for a type of system
encourages consistency across projects
cards.use: want several teams to follow the same proven pattern
not: is a diagram of one specific running system

cards.subject: single point of failure
says: is one component whose failure stops the whole system
is removed by adding redundancy
cards.use: find that one server going down would take the whole service offline
not: is a test that must pass before a release

cards.subject: high availability
says: is designing a system to keep running when parts fail
uses redundancy and automatic failover
cards.use: need a service to stay up even if a server fails
not: is making a system faster for a single user

cards.subject: legacy modernisation
says: updates or replaces old systems that still run the business
is often done in stages to limit risk
cards.use: need to move off an ageing system without stopping the business
not: is adding more features to a brand-new system

cards.subject: strangler fig pattern
says: replaces a legacy system piece by piece behind a common front
lets old and new run side by side until the old can be switched off
cards.use: want to replace a legacy system gradually rather than in one risky switch-over
not: rewrites the whole system and switches over in one big step

cards.subject: domain-driven design
says: structures software around the business domain and its language
splits systems into bounded contexts
cards.use: need software boundaries to follow how the business is organised
not: designs the whole database before any code is written

cards.subject: multi-tenancy
says: serves many customers from one shared instance of a system
keeps each customer's data separate
cards.use: need one platform to serve many customers cost-effectively
not: runs a separate copy of the system for each customer

cards.subject: cloud-native
says: builds software to exploit cloud features such as elasticity and managed services
often uses containers and automation
cards.use: want applications designed to scale and recover in the cloud
not: means a system hosted in the company's own data centre

cards.subject: multi-cloud
says: uses services from more than one cloud provider
can reduce dependence on one supplier but adds complexity
cards.use: want to avoid depending on a single cloud provider
not: means running everything in one data centre

cards.subject: DORA framework
says: defines four measures of software delivery performance
includes deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore service
cards.use: need research-backed measures of how well a team delivers
not: counts lines of code written per developer

cards.subject: lead time for changes
says: is the time from a code commit to running in production
is a DORA measure of delivery speed
cards.use: want to know how long a change takes to reach users after it is committed
not: is the share of releases that cause a failure

cards.subject: change failure rate
says: is the share of releases that cause a failure needing a fix
is a DORA measure of delivery quality
cards.use: want to know how often releases cause problems
not: is the time taken to recover from an outage

cards.subject: mean time to restore
says: is the average time taken to recover from a failure in production
is a DORA measure of resilience
cards.use: want to know how quickly service returns after an outage
not: is the share of releases that cause a failure

cards.subject: cycle time
says: is the time work takes from being started to being finished
shows where work waits
cards.use: want to see how long items take to finish once started
not: is the amount of work a team completes in an iteration

cards.subject: velocity
says: is the amount of work a team completes in an iteration
is meant for a team's own planning rather than comparing teams
cards.use: need a team to forecast what it can take on next sprint
not: is a measure of how quickly one individual writes code

cards.subject: Conway's law
says: says a system's design will mirror the communication structure of the organisation
is why team structure shapes architecture
cards.use: see system boundaries that match team boundaries
not: says that adding people to a late project makes it later

cards.subject: Team Topologies
says: offers four team types and three ways for teams to interact
aims to reduce the cognitive load on teams
cards.use: need a model for how teams should be shaped and interact
not: is a list of the servers used by each team

cards.subject: span of control
says: is the number of people who report directly to one manager
is set to balance support with the manager's workload
cards.use: need to decide how many people one manager should lead
not: is the range of tasks that one engineer can handle

cards.subject: on-call rotation
says: shares out responsibility for responding to production problems out of hours
needs fair scheduling and clear escalation
cards.use: need engineers to take turns responding to incidents
not: is a daily meeting of the whole team

cards.subject: psychological safety
says: is a shared belief that people can raise problems and ideas without being punished
is strongly linked with learning teams
cards.use: want people to admit mistakes and speak up
not: is the physical safety of an office

cards.subject: bus factor
says: is the number of people whose sudden absence would stop a project
is raised by spreading knowledge
cards.use: worry that one person's absence would halt a project
not: is how many releases a team ships per month

cards.subject: headcount
says: is the number of people employed or approved to be hired
is a main driver of people cost
cards.use: need to say how many people a team has or may hire
not: is the number of tasks in a backlog

cards.subject: attrition
says: is the rate at which people leave an organisation
can be measured for a team or for the whole organisation
cards.use: want to know how many people are leaving
not: is the time it takes to hire someone

cards.subject: succession planning
says: prepares people to take over key roles when they become vacant
reduces the risk when a leader leaves
cards.use: worry about who could replace a key leader who leaves
not: lists the tasks a leaver must hand over

cards.subject: skip-level meeting
says: is a meeting between a leader and people who report to their direct reports
helps leaders hear what is happening several levels down
cards.use: want to hear directly from people two levels below you
not: is a meeting between two people at the same level

cards.subject: career ladder
says: sets out the levels of a role and what is expected at each
makes promotion and pay decisions more consistent
cards.use: need clear expectations for each engineering level
not: is a list of open vacancies

cards.subject: performance improvement plan
says: sets out expectations and support for someone who is below the required standard
is time-limited and documented
cards.use: need to give someone a fair, documented chance to reach the standard
not: is a reward given for strong performance

cards.subject: 360 feedback
says: gathers views on a person from peers, reports and managers
gives a rounded picture of how they work
cards.use: want input on a leader from the people around them
not: is feedback given only by the person's manager

cards.subject: org design
says: shapes how teams, roles and reporting lines are arranged
aims to match structure to strategy
cards.use: need to reorganise teams to match a new strategy
not: is the layout of the office floor

cards.subject: CapEx
says: is spending on assets that provide value over several years
is recorded on the balance sheet and written off over time
cards.use: buy hardware or build an asset that will last for years
not: is the day-to-day cost of running the business

cards.subject: OpEx
says: is the day-to-day spending needed to run the business
includes subscriptions and cloud usage billed as it is used
cards.use: need to describe regular running costs such as subscriptions
not: is spending on long-lived assets

cards.subject: total cost of ownership
says: counts all the costs of a system across its life
includes running, support and exit costs as well as the purchase price
cards.use: need to compare two options over several years
not: is the price on a supplier's quote

cards.subject: return on investment
says: compares the benefit from an investment with its cost
is shown as a ratio or a percentage
cards.use: need to show whether a project is worth what it costs
not: is the total cost of owning a system

cards.subject: FinOps
says: manages cloud spending through shared accountability across engineering and finance
aims to get more value from every pound spent on cloud
cards.use: see cloud bills rising with nobody owning them
not: is a regulation that governs financial reporting

cards.subject: burn rate
says: is how fast an organisation spends its cash
is usually stated per month
cards.use: need to know how quickly cash is being used
not: is the speed at which a server uses power

cards.subject: runway
says: is how long an organisation can operate before its cash runs out
is calculated from the cash held and the burn rate
cards.use: need to know how many months the cash will last
not: is the rate at which cash is spent

cards.subject: unit economics
says: measures the revenue and cost for a single unit such as one customer
shows whether growth actually makes money
cards.use: need to know whether each customer is profitable
not: is the total profit across the whole business

cards.subject: cost of delay
says: estimates the value lost for each period a piece of work is late
helps order work by its economic urgency
cards.use: need to decide which of several projects to do first
not: is the penalty clause in a supplier contract

cards.subject: capitalised development cost
says: is development spending that accounting rules allow to be recorded as an asset
is written off over its useful life
cards.use: need to know when software development spending can be treated as an asset
not: is the running cost of a live service

cards.subject: risk register
says: is a list of identified risks with their owners and treatments
is reviewed regularly
cards.use: need one place that records risks and who owns them
not: is a log of past outages only

cards.subject: risk appetite
says: is the amount and type of risk an organisation is willing to accept
is set by the board or senior leaders
cards.use: need to decide how much risk the organisation will accept to pursue a goal
not: is the list of identified risks

cards.subject: recovery time objective
says: is the longest acceptable time for a system to be down after a failure
guides how much to invest in recovery
cards.use: need to say how quickly a system must be back after an outage
not: is the amount of data that may be lost

cards.subject: recovery point objective
says: is the most data loss, measured in time, that is acceptable
determines how often backups or replication must happen
cards.use: need to say how much recent data can be lost
not: is the longest acceptable downtime

cards.subject: business continuity plan
says: sets out how critical activities carry on during a disruption
covers people, premises, suppliers and technology
cards.use: need to keep critical services running during a major disruption
not: is a list of growth targets for the year

cards.subject: zero trust
says: assumes no user or device is trusted just because it is on the network
verifies every request explicitly
cards.use: want access decisions that do not trust the internal network
not: trusts anything inside the company firewall

cards.subject: defence in depth
says: uses several layers of security controls
means the failure of one layer does not expose everything
cards.use: want several overlapping protections instead of relying on one
not: relies on one strong perimeter firewall

cards.subject: penetration test
says: is an authorised simulated attack that looks for weaknesses
produces a report of findings to fix
cards.use: need to find out whether an attacker could break in
not: is a test of whether the system handles heavy traffic

cards.subject: ISO 27001
says: is an international standard for an information security management system
can be certified by an independent auditor
cards.use: need an internationally recognised security certification
not: is a report on a service provider's controls, issued by an auditor

cards.subject: SOC 2
says: is an independent report on a service provider's controls for security and related criteria
is often requested by customers when they buy software
cards.use: need to show customers an independent report on your security controls
not: is a standard that can be held only by government bodies

cards.subject: GDPR
says: is a data protection law that governs how personal data is handled
gives individuals rights over their data
cards.use: handle the personal data of people in Europe
not: applies only to companies that are based in the EU

cards.subject: data residency
says: is the requirement or choice to keep data in a particular country or region
can be driven by law, contract or customer demand
cards.use: need to keep customer data within a specific country
not: is the backup of data kept at a second site

cards.subject: data protection impact assessment
says: assesses the privacy risks of a proposed use of personal data before it begins
is required for processing that is likely to be high risk
cards.use: plan a new system that uses personal data in a risky way
not: tests software for security holes

cards.subject: data processing agreement
says: is a contract that sets how a supplier handles personal data on your behalf
is needed between a controller and a processor
cards.use: need a contract with a supplier that will process personal data for you
not: is a contract that sets how fast a supplier must respond

cards.subject: segregation of duties
says: splits key tasks between people so that no one can complete a risky process alone
reduces the chance of fraud and error
cards.use: need to stop one person both writing and approving a payment
not: gives one administrator control over every step of a process

cards.subject: change advisory board
says: reviews and approves significant changes to live systems
weighs the risk and timing of a change
cards.use: need a group to approve risky changes to production
not: is a team that writes the release notes

cards.subject: copyleft licence
says: requires that derived work is shared under the same licence terms
can affect whether you must publish your own code
cards.use: need to know whether using an open-source library forces you to open your own code
not: lets anyone use the code with no conditions at all

cards.subject: software bill of materials
says: lists the components and dependencies that make up a piece of software
helps find affected systems when a vulnerability is announced
cards.use: need to know whether a newly announced vulnerability affects your software
not: is the list of costs of building the software

cards.subject: intellectual property
says: is the legal rights over creations such as code, designs and inventions
may belong to the employer or to a contractor unless agreed otherwise
cards.use: need to know who owns the code written by a contractor
not: is the physical equipment that the company owns

cards.subject: source code escrow
says: is an arrangement where a third party holds a supplier's code
lets the customer obtain it if the supplier fails
cards.use: worry that a key software supplier might go out of business
not: is a backup of your own repositories

cards.subject: service level agreement
says: is a contract that sets the level of service a supplier will provide
often states remedies such as service credits
cards.use: need a supplier to commit to uptime and response times
not: is the internal target for how reliable a service should be

cards.subject: request for proposal
says: is a document that asks suppliers to bid to meet stated requirements
lets a buyer compare offers on the same basis
cards.use: need several suppliers to bid for the same requirement
not: is a small trial to test a technology

cards.subject: proof of concept
says: is a small trial to show that an idea or technology can work
is done before committing to a full project
cards.use: want to test whether a technology works before buying it
not: is a document inviting suppliers to bid

cards.subject: master services agreement
says: sets the general legal terms that apply to all work between two parties
lets later work be agreed in short orders under those terms
cards.use: need standard legal terms that cover a long-term relationship with a supplier
not: describes one specific piece of work and its price

cards.subject: statement of work
says: describes the specific work, deliverables and price for one engagement
sits under the general terms of a master agreement
cards.use: need to define exactly what a supplier will deliver for a project
not: sets the general legal terms for all future work

cards.subject: exit strategy
says: is the plan for leaving a supplier or system without losing data or service
is best agreed before a contract is signed
cards.use: need to know how you would leave a supplier if things go wrong
not: is the plan for when a senior employee retires

cards.subject: shelfware
says: is software that is paid for but hardly used
wastes licence spend
cards.use: find that many paid licences are never used
not: is software that is stored in a data centre

cards.subject: nearshoring
says: moves work to a supplier in a nearby country or time zone
eases collaboration compared with distant locations
cards.use: want outsourced work done by a team in a similar time zone
not: moves work back to the home country

cards.subject: managed service
says: is a service in which a supplier runs and maintains a system for you
is paid for as an ongoing service
cards.use: want a supplier to run and look after a system for you
not: is software that you install and operate yourself

cards.subject: vendor due diligence
says: checks a supplier's finances, security and capability before a contract
reduces the risk of choosing a weak supplier
cards.use: need to check that a supplier is sound before signing
not: is a review of your own team's performance

cards.subject: data governance
says: sets who owns data, how it is defined and who may use it
covers quality, access and compliance
cards.use: need clear ownership and rules for the organisation's data
not: is the storage hardware for the data

cards.subject: data warehouse
says: stores structured, cleaned data organised for reporting and analysis
brings data from many source systems together
cards.use: need one place for clean, structured data for reports
not: stores raw data in any format with no set structure

cards.subject: data lake
says: stores large amounts of raw data in its original form
defers deciding on a structure until the data is used
cards.use: need to keep raw data of many types for later use
not: holds only cleaned, structured data for reporting

cards.subject: data quality
says: is how accurate, complete and consistent data is
limits how far analytics and AI can be trusted
cards.use: find that reports disagree because the data is wrong or missing
not: is how much data an organisation holds

cards.subject: large language model
says: is a model trained on large amounts of text to generate and understand language
predicts likely next tokens
cards.use: need to describe the technology behind a modern AI assistant
not: is a database that stores documents

cards.subject: hallucination
says: is when an AI model produces confident but false output
is reduced by grounding answers in trusted sources
cards.use: see an AI assistant invent a source that does not exist
not: is when a model refuses to answer

cards.subject: retrieval-augmented generation
says: fetches relevant documents and adds them to a model's prompt
grounds answers in your own up-to-date data
cards.use: want an AI assistant to answer from your company documents
not: retrains the model from scratch on your data

cards.subject: prompt injection
says: is an attack where text in the input tricks a model into ignoring its instructions
is a risk when a model reads untrusted content
cards.use: worry that a web page a model reads could carry hidden instructions
not: is a way of writing better prompts

cards.subject: model drift
says: is when a model's accuracy falls because real-world data changes over time
is caught by monitoring performance
cards.use: see a model's accuracy fall as customer behaviour changes
not: is a model being deleted from production

cards.subject: human in the loop
says: keeps a person reviewing or approving an automated or AI decision
reduces the risk from mistakes in high-stakes decisions
cards.use: need a person to approve an AI recommendation before it affects a customer
not: lets an AI act with no review at all

cards.subject: board pack
says: is the set of papers sent to board members before a meeting
summarises performance, risks and decisions needed
cards.use: need to prepare material for a board meeting
not: is the set of minutes written after a meeting

cards.subject: audit committee
says: is a board committee that oversees financial reporting, risk and internal control
receives reports from auditors
cards.use: need to report on controls and risks to a committee of the board
not: is a team of external auditors

cards.subject: technical due diligence
says: is an independent review of a company's technology, team and risks
is done before an investment or an acquisition
cards.use: face an investor reviewing your technology before a deal
not: is a review of the finances of a supplier

cards.subject: steering committee
says: is a group of senior stakeholders that guides a major project
makes decisions that the project team cannot
cards.use: need senior stakeholders to guide a big programme
not: is the team that does the day-to-day work

cards.subject: RACI
says: is a matrix that shows who is responsible, accountable, consulted and informed
clarifies who does what on a piece of work
cards.use: need to clear up who owns a decision
not: is a ranking of risks by cost

cards.subject: operating model
says: describes how an organisation arranges people, process and technology to deliver value
links strategy to day-to-day work
cards.use: need to describe how the organisation works to deliver its strategy
not: is a forecast of next year's revenue

cards.subject: digital transformation
says: changes how an organisation works by using digital technology
involves process and culture change as well as technology
cards.use: are asked to change how a whole organisation works through technology
not: is replacing office computers with new ones

cards.subject: change management
says: helps people adopt a change in the way they work
covers communication, training and support
cards.use: need people to adopt a new system or way of working
not: is the approval of changes to live servers

cards.subject: business case
says: sets out the reasons, costs, benefits and risks of a proposal
is used to decide whether to go ahead
cards.use: need to persuade leaders to fund a project
not: is a plan for how a project will be tested

cards.subject: post-merger integration
says: combines the systems, teams and processes of two organisations after a deal
often decides whether the deal's expected value is achieved
cards.use: need to merge the technology of two companies after an acquisition
not: is the review done before a deal is agreed

qa.q: What best describes a roadmap?
qa.right: The planned direction and sequence of work, which changes as priorities change
wrong: A fixed contract of dates and features
A list of every bug found
qa.why: A roadmap is a plan for outcomes, not a fixed contract.

qa.q: A supplier commits in a contract to 99.9 per cent uptime. What is this contract term called?
qa.why: An SLA sets the service a supplier will provide.

qa.q: Two teams each think the other owns a decision. Which tool helps clear it up?
qa.why: A RACI shows who is responsible, accountable, consulted and informed.

qa.q: You want to test whether a new technology works before buying it. What do you run?
qa.why: A proof of concept is a small trial before commitment.

qa.q: An engineer hides a mistake because they fear being blamed. What is lacking?
qa.why: People need to feel safe to admit mistakes.

qa.q: Where do you record a newly spotted risk and its owner?
qa.why: A risk register lists risks with owners and treatments.

qa.q: Which measure compares the benefit of a project with its cost?
qa.why: ROI compares benefit with cost.

qa.q: One server going down would take the whole service offline. What is this?
qa.why: A single point of failure stops everything when it fails.

qa.q: A new system launches but staff keep using the old spreadsheet. Which discipline was neglected?
qa.why: Change management helps people adopt new ways of working.

qa.q: Only one engineer understands how billing works. What risk is this?
qa.why: Knowledge held by one person is a bus factor risk.

qa.q: You need to persuade leaders to fund a project. What do you prepare?
qa.why: A business case sets out costs, benefits and risks.

qa.q: Which technology generates language after being trained on large amounts of text?
qa.why: An LLM is trained on text to generate language.

qa.q: Which DORA measure is the share of releases that cause a failure needing a fix?
qa.why: Change failure rate measures delivery quality.

qa.q: The business can accept losing at most 15 minutes of data. Which objective is that?
qa.why: RPO is the acceptable data loss measured in time.

qa.q: A system must be back within two hours of a failure. Which objective is that?
qa.why: RTO is the longest acceptable downtime.

qa.q: Option A is cheaper to buy but costs far more to run and to leave. Which measure gives the fair comparison?
qa.why: Total cost of ownership counts all costs over the life.

qa.q: A tool is needed by everyone but gives the company no advantage. What is the usual approach?
qa.right: Buy it rather than build it
wrong: Put it on the technology radar as hold
qa.why: Commodity capability is usually bought; build the differentiating parts.

qa.q: An AI assistant invents a source that does not exist. What is this?
qa.why: A hallucination is a confident but false output.

qa.q: Analysts need clean, structured data for monthly reports. Where should it live?
qa.why: A warehouse holds structured, cleaned data for reporting.

qa.q: You want to find out whether an attacker could break into your systems. What do you commission?
qa.why: A penetration test simulates an authorised attack.

qa.q: A manager has 20 direct reports and struggles to support them. What is the issue?
qa.right: The span of control is too wide
wrong: The bus factor is too high
qa.why: Too many direct reports overloads a manager.

qa.q: A contractor wrote core code but the contract is silent on ownership. What is the risk?
qa.right: Unclear ownership of the intellectual property
qa.why: Unless agreed, ownership may sit with the contractor.

qa.q: Many paid licences are never used. What do you call this?
qa.why: Shelfware is paid for but hardly used.

qa.q: You want several overlapping security protections, not just a perimeter firewall. Which approach is that?
qa.why: Defence in depth uses several layers.

qa.q: Your system boundaries keep matching team boundaries. Which idea explains this?
qa.why: Systems mirror the communication structure of the organisation.

qa.q: An assistant must answer from the latest company policies without retraining. What do you use?
qa.why: RAG adds relevant documents to the prompt.

qa.q: A web page that a model reads contains hidden instructions that change the model's behaviour. What is this attack?
qa.why: Untrusted text tricks the model into ignoring its instructions.

qa.q: An AI recommendation will affect a customer's credit. What control reduces the risk of mistakes?
qa.right: A human in the loop who approves it
qa.why: A person reviews high-stakes decisions.

qa.q: Cloud bills keep rising and nobody owns them. Which practice should you adopt?
qa.why: FinOps creates shared accountability for cloud spend.

qa.q: A company has six million in cash and spends half a million a month. What is its runway?
qa.why: Cash divided by monthly spend gives the runway.

qa.q: A customer demands that their data stays inside one country. Which concept is this?
qa.why: Data residency keeps data in a region.

qa.q: A new system will profile customers using personal data in a high-risk way. What should happen before launch?
qa.why: A DPIA assesses privacy risks before processing starts.

qa.q: One person can both write and approve a payment. Which control would prevent this?
qa.why: Splitting tasks stops one person completing a risky process alone.

qa.q: Enterprise customers ask for an independent report on your security controls. Which is most likely to be requested?
qa.why: SOC 2 is an independent report on a provider's controls.

qa.q: Before signing with a new supplier you want to know how you would leave them. What do you agree?
qa.why: An exit strategy is agreed before the contract is signed.

qa.q: The board says it will accept some risk in new markets but none with customer data. What has it defined?
qa.why: Risk appetite is the amount and type of risk it will accept.

qa.q: Which action best helps a senior leader hear what is happening two levels down?
qa.why: Skip-level meetings reach people who report to your reports.

qa.q: An investor wants an independent review of your technology, team and risks before a deal. What is that?
qa.why: Technical due diligence happens before a deal.

qa.q: Two projects cost the same: A saves 10,000 a month and B earns 100,000 a month. Using cost of delay, which should go first?
qa.right: B, because each month of delay loses more value
wrong: Either, because the cost is the same
Neither, until there is more budget
qa.why: Cost of delay orders work by value lost per period.

qa.q: A critical library vulnerability is announced. What helps you find which systems are affected quickly?
qa.why: An SBOM lists components and dependencies.

qa.q: You need to replace a legacy system without one risky switch-over. Which pattern fits?
qa.why: The old system is replaced piece by piece.

qa.q: A key software supplier may go out of business and you depend on their code. What protection could you arrange?
qa.why: Escrow lets you obtain the code if the supplier fails.

qa.q: Software development spending can be treated as an asset under accounting rules. What is it called?
qa.why: It is recorded as an asset and written off over its life.

qa.q: Teams are overloaded by too many responsibilities. Which model aims to reduce cognitive load?
qa.why: Team Topologies shapes teams to reduce cognitive load.

qa.q: A model's accuracy falls as customer behaviour changes. What is this?
qa.why: Real-world data changes over time.

qa.q: After buying a company you need to combine its systems, teams and processes with yours. What is this?
qa.why: Integration follows the deal and decides whether the expected value is achieved.

qa.q: You want to see how components of your technology are evolving and where to invest. Which tool helps?
qa.why: A Wardley map shows evolution of components.

qa.q: Software boundaries should follow how the business is organised, with bounded contexts. Which approach is this?
qa.why: Domain-driven design structures software around the business domain.

qa.q: A board asks who will take over if the head of engineering leaves unexpectedly. Which practice answers this?
qa.why: Succession planning prepares replacements for key roles.

qa.q: The CTO is asked why the organisation cannot simply compare team productivity by velocity. What is the best answer?
qa.right: Velocity is meant for a team's own planning and is not comparable across teams
wrong: Velocity is banned by the DORA framework
qa.why: Velocity is a team-level planning measure.
